headline: Local Woman's 'Tongue-Tap' InstaSnap Method Goes Viral, Dermatologists Concerned
subheadline: Hands-free scrolling technique sparks hygiene debate across multiple platforms
summary: A Millbrook resident's viral ClipTok demonstrating how she double-taps InstaSnap photos with her tongue has sparked both imitation and medical concern.
content:
What started as a convenience hack has become a full-blown social media phenomenon, and local dermatologists are not amused.

Miranda Chu, 24, posted a ClipTok video last Tuesday showing her technique for liking InstaSnap photos while eating a burrito with both hands. The method involves extending her tongue to tap the screen twice in rapid succession.

"I call it the 'Tongue-Tap,'" Chu explained in a follow-up video that has now accumulated over 847,000 views. "My hands are always busy. Eating, holding my cat, applying face masks. But my tongue is just sitting there doing nothing most of the time."

The video has spawned thousands of imitation attempts, with users sharing their own tongue-tapping techniques under the hashtag #TongueTapChallenge. Some have refined the method further, with one user claiming they can scroll, like, and comment using only their tongue.

Dr. Patricia Vance, a dermatologist at Millbrook General Hospital, has seen an uptick in facial acne cases she attributes directly to the trend.

"Phone screens harbor approximately 17,000 different types of bacteria," Dr. Vance stated during a press conference. "We're seeing cases of perioral dermatitis that patients are calling 'phone mouth.' This is not a term I ever expected to use in my medical career."

Device repair shops have also noticed an increase in water damage claims.

"People are coming in with phones that smell like salsa," reported Techwiz Repairs technician Derek Morrison. "I've had to implement a 'visible moisture policy.' If I can see it glisten, I'm charging extra."

Chu remains unapologetic. In her latest update, she revealed she's been tongue-tapping for 847 days straight.

"People say it's gross, but those same people lick envelopes and share drinks," she argued. "At least I'm the only one licking my phone. Usually."

InstaSnap has not issued an official statement but quietly pushed an update last week adding an accessibility feature for hands-free liking using voice commands. Industry analysts suggest this was not a coincidence.

The #TongueTapChallenge continues to spread, with variations now appearing on VidTube and Chirper.
author: Jasper Holloway, Digital Trends
